record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: For a combinatorial graph G, define the treewidth of its continuous counterpart Γ(G) to be the 1-bramble number of Γ(G), where a 1-bramble is a family of subtrees of Γ(G) any two of which come within distance 1, and the order of the bramble is the minimum size of a point set hitting every subtree in the family. Is there a tractable algorithm that, given a continuous graph and a fixed small integer k > 0, decides whether its 1-bramble number is at most k?

evidence.quote: Definition 13. The treewidth of a continuous graph Γ(G) is the 1-bramble number of Γ(G).

On the other hand, recognizing whether the 1-bramble number of a continuous graph is at most k, for a given small integer k > 0, might be a very challenging and not necessarily tractable problem. We leave this as an open problem of this section.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph. The continuous graph Γ(G) associated with G is the topological space obtained from G by viewing each edge uv ∈ E as a homeomorphic copy of the unit interval [0,1] whose endpoints are identified with the vertices u and v, equipped with the path metric in which every edge has length 1; points of Γ(G) include all vertices of G and all interior points of its edges.

A subtree of Γ(G) is a non-empty, compact, connected subset of Γ(G) that contains no homeomorphic image of a circle. For two subsets A, B ⊆ Γ(G), let d(A,B) = inf{ d(a,b) : a ∈ A, b ∈ B } denote the infimum of distances under the path metric.

A 1-bramble of Γ(G) is a family F of subtrees of Γ(G) such that for every T, T' ∈ F one has d(T, T') ≤ 1. A hitting set for F is a set S ⊆ Γ(G) such that S ∩ T ≠ ∅ for every T ∈ F. The order of F is the minimum cardinality of a hitting set for F. The 1-bramble number of Γ(G), denoted bn₁(Γ(G)), is the supremum of the orders of all 1-brambles of Γ(G); this quantity is taken to be the treewidth of the continuous graph Γ(G).

Problem. For each fixed positive integer k, design an algorithm (or determine the computational complexity of the problem) that, given a finite simple graph G as input, decides whether bn₁(Γ(G)) ≤ k. In particular, is this decision problem solvable in polynomial time (or otherwise tractable) for every fixed small k > 0?
